title.narrative: Managing Public Resources for Service Delivery

description.narrative: The Project Development Objective (PDO) is to improve domestic tax management, budget execution, and transparency and accountability in the management of public resources.

The development objective of the Managing Public Resources for Service Delivery Project for Mozambique is to improve domestic tax management, budget execution, and transparency and accountability in the management of public resources. The project comprises of five components. The first component is strengthening domestic tax management. It consists of following sub-components: (i) reinforcing tax administration; and (ii) incentives for strengthening domestic revenue management. The second component is enhancing public expenditure management and control. It consists of following sub-components: (i) institutional capacity building for the Ministry of Economy and Finance (MEF); (ii) strengthening internal audit arrangements; and (iii) incentives for improved expenditure management and control. The third component is improving independent external oversight. It consists of following sub-components: (i) support for external audit; (ii) enhancing social accountability and citizen engagement; and (iii) strengthening state-owned enterprise (SOE) oversight. The fourth component is project management. The project will also hire an independent verification agent for the purpose of certifying the achievement of the performance-based condition (PBC) targets annually. The fifth component, contingency emergency response component (CERC) will facilitate access to rapid financing by reallocating uncommitted project funds in the event of a natural disaster, either by a formal declaration of a national or regional emergency or upon a formal request from the Government of Mozambique (GoM).

title.narrative: Tax base broadened through integrated taxpayer registries and online filing and payment of tax

baseline.value: Tax systems and databases are not integrated; Limited functionality of online taxpayer portal

target.value: E-tributação system expanded so that the following taxes are operational throughout the country: SISA, Tax on Sucessions and Donations, Tax on National Reconstruction, Vehicles Tax; Online filing and payment operational for the following 8 taxes — VAT, ISPC, IRPC, IRPS, mining production, oil production, surface, and oil yield —operational;

comment.narrative: The corresponding amount was disbursed (1.25M)

actual.value: The goal of year 1 was fully achieved, with the inclusion of the following taxes in the E-taxation system: SISA, Inheritance and Gift Tax, National Reconstruction Tax, and Vehicle Tax; the goal of year 2 was partially achieved, with the operational online declaration and payment of the following taxes — VAT, ISPC, IRPC, IRPS, mining production, oil production, surface and oil revenue — but without integration and interoperability between the E-taxation and Single Electronic Window (JUE) systems.

title.narrative: Current expenditure outturn as percentage of approved budget amount

comment.narrative: As of September 30, 2025, the current expenditure outturn was 70.2%, slightly below the expenditure outturn in September 2024 (73.0%) due to delays in paying salaries for September of the current year. The annual target of reducing overspending from 111% to at least 104% is likely to be met given that the government expects to limit new hires and retiring staff who have reached the eligible age.

title.narrative: Investment expenditure outturn as a percentage of approved budget amount

comment.narrative: From January 1 to September 30, 2025, investment expenditure execution stands at 34.1% of the approved budget, representing a decrease of 2.4 percentage points compared to the corresponding period in 2024. The domestic investment component had higher execution (58.7%) than the external component (26.2%). It is unlikely that the government will reach this indicator's target by the end of the year.Significant part of the foreign investment component continues to be off-single treasury account. This requires manual incorporation of balance sheets. The GoM expects to have final figures for 2025 by early March, 2026, and this indicator is likely to improve.

As of September 30, 2025, 68.4 percent of the approved budgeted revenues had been collected, the same performance level recorded in the corresponding period of 2024. However, given the nature of budget execution, this indicator is assessed more meaningfully only after data for the full year becomes available. The government's baseline scenario is that the 94% target will be reached by the end of the year. According to the communiquE of the 40th Ordinary Session of the Council of Ministers, revenue collection in 2025 is expected to total around MZN 361.8 billion - about MZN 24.0 billion below the initial forecast, but slightly above the 94% target.

baseline.value: Transfers to provinces and municipalities are neither transparent nor predictable nor timely.

target.value: Transfers to provinces and municipalities were executed fully in a way that was transparent and timely.

comment.narrative: The target has been largely met.

actual.value: The Ministry of Finance (MF) published on its website information on fiscal transfers to provinces and local governments, including: (i) the amounts planned and actually transferred, disaggregated by province and municipality; and (ii) the transfer formulas, with the respective data and sources used. PBC 3 was largely met, meeting the criteria of transparency and timeliness. As for predictability, although total transfers to provinces and local governments exceeded by 121.1% the amount authorized in the Budget Law, there were cases of over-allocation and under-allocation - especially among local governments - in disagreement with prevailing limits, which negatively affected the predictability of the transfers.
